source.title: Towards Bridging the Performance Gaps of Joint Energy-Based Models
source.authors: Xiulong Yang; Qing Su; Shihao Ji

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether adding sharpness-aware optimization and changing data augmentation affect classification performance, but does not test any listed version's specific claim or measure.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR10 ablation reports classification accuracy after SAM and data-augmentation changes, but no training error or train-test gap. The paper's landscape visualizations and generalization discussion do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Other classification, generation, calibration, OOD, and robustness comparisons do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization rationale to motivate SAM and reports its method's performance. It tests none of V1–V8. In particular, energy-landscape visualizations and SAM/ASAM accuracy comparisons do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training–test gaps, or ranking against other generalization measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute smoother energy landscapes and improved generalization to SAM and removing augmentation from the likelihood branch, and report improved performance across several tasks. Their generalization explanation is an interpretation rather than a measured sharpness–gap relationship. Robustness gains also require qualification: Section 4.4 reports robustness similar to JEM overall, with advantages at smaller SGLD step counts.
record.recipe_differences: The study modifies JEM/JEM++ training by adding SAM and separating augmented classification data from unaugmented likelihood data; it does not use the original studies' random-label, width-sweep, optimizer-comparison, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-gap, or memorized-example-removal recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of SGLD steps K changes reported classification accuracy, generation quality, calibration, and robustness; the paper also reports a cosine learning-rate scheduler improves CIFAR10 accuracy and FID for SADA-JEM.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 reports JEM accuracy increasing from 89.5% to 90.1% with SAM and JEM++ accuracy increasing from 93.5% to 94.1%; SADA-JEM reaches 96.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM and the SADA-JEM training recipe improve reported CIFAR10 classification accuracy in these comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing augmentation from the likelihood branch gives 93.6% accuracy versus 93.5% for JEM++; adding energy L2 regularization gives 93.4% and fails to maintain realistic image generation after 110 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Likelihood-branch augmentation removal mainly improves generation quality here; energy L2 regularization does not improve classification accuracy or stabilize generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1 and 7 visualize smoother energy landscapes for SADA-JEM. Appendix C defines the plotted quantity as summed energy on a random 10% of CIFAR10 training examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SADA-JEM changes the geometry of the plotted energy surface; this does not establish the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

record.problems: The ablation table reports no uncertainty, training error, or explicit test-set designation for its accuracy values, so it cannot establish a train-test gap or connect landscape smoothness to that gap.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Other reported results concern generation quality, calibration, OOD detection, or adversarial robustness rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own finding that no listed version is tested. ASAM's magnitude-dependent optimization rule in Section 3 and its performance sweep in Table 6 do not supply V7's required measurement. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization using the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the effect of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum under different tuning and regularization choices.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adjusted recipes.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, training-error rise, and ranking of train-test gaps against other measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: JEM
rows.operation_detail: JEM training without SAM; CIFAR10 ablation
rows.note: Training error and the test-set designation are not reported for this ablation.
rows.check: The 89.5% accuracy matches Table 5, but this is a method-performance comparator outside all listed versions.

rows.subject: JEM +SAM
rows.note: The paper describes SAM as improving classification accuracy; training error and the test-set designation are not reported for this ablation.
rows.check: The increase from 89.5% to 90.1% matches Table 5. Adding SAM does not test V7's sharpness–gap correlation.

rows.subject: JEM++
rows.operation_detail: JEM++ training without SAM; CIFAR10 ablation
rows.note: Training error and the test-set designation are not reported for this ablation.
rows.check: The 93.5% accuracy matches Table 5, but this is a method-performance comparator outside all listed versions.

rows.subject: JEM++ +SAM
rows.note: The paper describes SAM as improving classification accuracy; training error and the test-set designation are not reported for this ablation.
rows.check: The increase from 93.5% to 94.1% matches Table 5. Neither perturbation tolerance nor the generalization gap is measured.

rows.subject: JEM++ w/o DA
rows.note: Training error and the test-set designation are not reported for this ablation.
rows.check: The 93.6% accuracy matches Table 5. Only likelihood-branch augmentation is removed; classification augmentation remains. This does not test V6's dropout or joint dropout/weight-decay removal.

rows.subject: JEM++ w/o DA +L2
rows.stage_stated: failed to generate realistic images after 110 epochs
rows.operation_detail: JEM++ without data augmentation with energy L2 regularization instead of SAM
rows.note: The paper states this configuration fails to generate realistic images after 110 epochs; training error and the test-set designation are not reported.
rows.check: The 93.4% accuracy matches Table 5. The regularizer acts on sample energy magnitudes, rather than being a dropout/weight-decay comparison. Failure to generate realistic images after 110 epochs does not establish that classification training stopped then.

rows.subject: SADA-JEM
rows.operation_detail: SAM with data augmentation retained for classification and excluded from the likelihood pipeline
rows.note: This combines SAM and removal of augmentation from pθ(T(x)); training error and the test-set designation are not reported.
rows.check: The 96.0% accuracy matches Table 5 but measures the proposed method's performance. Appendix A also identifies cosine scheduling as available to SADA-JEM while other ablations are insufficiently stable; the improvement cannot safely be attributed solely to SAM and augmentation changes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
